title: Homology of an exponent-vector Cech subcomplex
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $n\ge1$, $e\in\mathbf Z^{n+1}$, and $N_e=\{i:e_i<0\}$. Let $C_e^ ullet$ be the cochain complex whose degree-$p$ term is the free $A$-module on the subsets $J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n\}$ with $|J|=p+1$ and $J\supseteq N_e$, with the alternating differential $d[J]=\sum_{k

source.place: Tag 01XS, label lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring, proof: NEG(e) cases and contracting homotopy

proof.text: If N_e is empty, the basis consists of all nonempty subsets of {0,...,n}. The usual augmented simplex calculation, obtained by inserting the vertex 0 with the alternating sign, gives d^2=0, identifies the kernel in degree 0 with the constant coefficient copy of A, and gives a contracting homotopy in every positive degree. Thus H^0 is A and all other cohomology vanishes.

If N_e is nonempty and proper, choose r outside N_e and define h on a basis [J] by h[J]=0 when r is not in J and h[J]=(-1)^{#\{j\in J:j<r\}}[J\setminus\{r\}] when r is in J. Expanding d h+h d on [J], the terms indexed by k other than r cancel in pairs with opposite signs, while the r-term is [J]; hence d h+h d=id. Since h lowers degree and C^{-1}=0, this identity makes every cocycle a coboundary, including degree zero, so all H^q vanish. This is the explicit contracting-homotopy calculation in Tag 01XS.

source.place: Tag 01XS, proof: contracting homotopy for nonempty proper NEG(e)

proof.text: If N_e is the full index set, the only allowed subset is the full set itself, in degree n. Therefore C_e^n is the free rank-one A-module generated by [ {0,...,n} ], every other term is zero, and all differentials are zero. This gives H^n=A·[ {0,...,n} ] and zero cohomology in other degrees.
